ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.error: Thinks a toothbrush can be shared with a brother or sister if it is rinsed.

example.question: Can you share your toothbrush with your sister?
example.correct_answer: No, a toothbrush is a personal item

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.cause: Sharing is praised at home, so sharing everything seems kind.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Yes, if we rinse it" beside "No, a toothbrush is a personal item" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.help: Sort items into "mine only" and "for everyone". Say: some things carry germs from one mouth to another.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.feedback: A toothbrush is a personal item. We do not share it, even with family.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.error: Calls an item personal because he uses it most, such as the family chair he likes.

example.question: Is the sofa at home a personal item or a common item?
example.correct_answer: Common, everyone uses it

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.cause: The child thinks "personal" means "the one I like" or "I use".
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Personal, I sit on it" beside "Common, everyone uses it" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.help: Ask: who else uses it? If many people use it, it is common.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.feedback: An item everyone at home uses is a common item.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.error: Thinks water alone is enough to clean greasy plates and dirty clothes.

example.question: What do you need to clean an oily plate?
example.correct_answer: Water and soap (or ash)

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.cause: Water makes things look wet and clean.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Only water" beside "Water and soap (or ash)" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.help: Wash one oily plate with water only and one with soap. Feel both.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.feedback: Oily plates need water and soap or ash to get clean.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.error: Thinks a towel is a common item because it hangs in a shared place.

example.question: Is your bathing towel a personal or common item?
example.wrong_answer: Common, it hangs where everyone bathes
example.correct_answer: Personal

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.cause: Where an item is kept decides, for the child, whose it is.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Common, it hangs where everyone bathes" beside "Personal" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.help: Ask what the towel touches: your body. Items that touch the body are personal.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.feedback: A bathing towel touches your body, so it is personal.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_HOME.HOME_ITEMS.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks anything he likes very much is a need.

example.question: Is a sweet a need or a want?
example.correct_answer: A want

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: For a young child, wanting something strongly feels the same as needing it.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "A need, I like sweets" beside "A want" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Ask: can we live well without it? Sort sweets, water, a toy and a blanket.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: A need is something we cannot live well without. Sweets are a want.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks expensive items are needs and cheap items are wants.

example.question: Which is a need: a television or a bag of maize flour?
example.correct_answer: Maize flour

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: Big prices make an item seem important.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "The television, it costs more" beside "Maize flour" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Compare prices and ask which we need to eat today. Price does not decide.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: A need is about living well, not about price. Food is a need.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Chooses a want first when there is only a little money.

example.question: Mother has 100 shillings. Should she buy soda or vegetables for supper?
example.correct_answer: Vegetables for supper

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: The child picks what is most exciting now.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "Soda" beside "Vegetables for supper" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Role-play shopping with play money: needs first, then a want if money is left.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: When money is little, we buy needs first. Wants can wait.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks school is a want, not a need, because some children do not go.

example.question: Is going to school a need or a want?
example.correct_answer: A need

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: The child has seen children out of school and thinks it is optional.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "A want" beside "A need" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Say: every child needs to learn, it is a child's right too. Link with Child Rights.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: Going to school is a need for every child.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks every need is met at a shop, including health care and learning.

example.question: Where does a sick child go to get treated?
example.correct_answer: A clinic or hospital

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: The child has seen medicine bought at a chemist and thinks shops do everything.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "A shop, to buy medicine" beside "A clinic or hospital" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Match cards: clinic and nurse, school and teacher, shop and food. A nurse checks the child first.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: A sick child goes to a clinic or hospital to see a nurse or doctor.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher (SAFE: child-safety content, read first): a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks food comes only from shops, not from farms and gardens.

example.question: Where else can a family get sukuma wiki apart from the shop?
example.correct_answer: From their own garden or a farm

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: A town child sees food only in shops.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "Nowhere, only the shop" beside "From their own garden or a farm" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Show a kitchen garden and a farm. Food grows first, then reaches the shop.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: Food grows on farms and in gardens before it reaches the shop.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks each place meets only one need.

example.question: Which needs can a market meet?
example.correct_answer: Food, clothes and household items

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: Matching games pair one item with one place.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "Only food" beside "Food, clothes and household items" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Walk through a picture of a market: food, clothes, utensils. One place, many needs.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: One place can meet many needs. A market sells food, clothes and more.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.error: Thinks water comes only from a tap.

example.question: Name a place apart from a tap where families get water.
example.correct_answer: A well, borehole, river or water tank

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.cause: Many children see only taps at school.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.reveals: Offer "There is none" beside "A well, borehole, river or water tank" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.help: Show pictures of a borehole, a well, a river and a roof tank.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.feedback: Families get water from taps, wells, boreholes, rivers and tanks.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.FAMILY_NEEDS_AND_WANTS.NE.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.error: Thinks cleaning the school is only the job of the school workers.

example.question: Who should keep our classroom clean?
example.correct_answer: All of us, pupils and workers

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.cause: The child sees paid workers sweeping and thinks it is not his duty.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.reveals: Offer "Only the cleaner" beside "All of us, pupils and workers" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.help: Make a class duty rota. Everyone keeps the class clean.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.feedback: Keeping our school clean is everyone's job, pupils too.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.error: Thinks a small sweet paper can be dropped on the ground because it is small.

example.question: Where should a sweet paper go?
example.wrong_answer: On the ground, it is small
example.correct_answer: In the dustbin or litter pit

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.cause: One small paper seems to make no difference.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.reveals: Offer "On the ground, it is small" beside "In the dustbin or litter pit" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.help: Drop one paper each for the class: count how many. Small litter adds up.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.feedback: Every piece of litter goes in the bin, even a small one.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.error: Sweeps without sprinkling water, raising dust, and thinks that is proper cleaning.

example.question: Before sweeping a dusty floor, what should you do?
example.correct_answer: Sprinkle a little water first

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.reveals: Offer "Sweep quickly" beside "Sprinkle a little water first" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.help: Sweep a dusty corner dry and wet. See the dust cloud. Dust makes us cough.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.feedback: Sprinkle a little water before sweeping so the dust does not rise.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.error: Thinks hands need washing after the toilet only if they look dirty.

example.question: When must you wash your hands at school?
example.correct_answer: After visiting the toilet and before eating

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.reveals: Offer "Only when they look dirty" beside "After visiting the toilet and before eating" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.help: Use glitter as "germs" on hands and see how they spread. Wash with soap.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.feedback: Always wash hands with soap after the toilet and before eating.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_CLEAN.M.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.error: Thinks accidents just happen by bad luck and cannot be prevented.

example.question: Can we prevent falls in the classroom?
example.correct_answer: Yes, by walking and keeping the floor dry and clear

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.cause: The word accident sounds like something nobody can control.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.reveals: Offer "No, accidents just happen" beside "Yes, by walking and keeping the floor dry and clear" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.help: For each accident card, ask: what could we do first so it does not happen?
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.feedback: Many accidents can be prevented. Walk, keep floors clear and report dangers.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher (SAFE: child-safety content, read first): a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.error: Thinks a child who is hurt should hide it so as not to get into trouble.

example.question: You cut your hand on a broken window. What do you do?
example.wrong_answer: Hide it so I am not punished
example.correct_answer: Tell a teacher at once

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.cause: The child fears blame for breaking a rule.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.reveals: Offer "Hide it so I am not punished" beside "Tell a teacher at once" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.help: Say clearly: when you are hurt, always tell a teacher. You will be helped.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.feedback: If you get hurt, tell a teacher straight away. They will help you.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher (SAFE: child-safety content, read first): a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.error: Thinks he should pick up broken glass himself to help.

example.question: You see broken glass on the path. What do you do?
example.wrong_answer: Pick it up with my hands
example.correct_answer: Keep others away and tell a teacher

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.cause: Helping is praised, so picking it up seems good.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.reveals: Offer "Pick it up with my hands" beside "Keep others away and tell a teacher" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.help: Role-play: stand near, warn friends, call a teacher. Adults pick up glass.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.feedback: Do not pick broken glass. Warn others and tell a teacher.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher (SAFE: child-safety content, read first): a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.error: Thinks running in corridors is safe if you are careful.

example.question: Is it safe to run in the corridor?
example.correct_answer: No, walk in the corridor

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.cause: Running is fun and the child feels in control.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.reveals: Offer "Yes, if I am careful" beside "No, walk in the corridor" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.help: Show how a corner hides someone coming. Practise walking in corridors.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.feedback: Walk in corridors. Running can make you knock into someone.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_SCHOOL.SCHOOL_ACCIDEN.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher (SAFE: child-safety content, read first): a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.error: Thinks red on the flag means danger because red means danger on signs.

example.question: What does red stand for on the Kenya flag?
example.correct_answer: The blood shed in the struggle for independence

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.cause: Red on signs and lights means stop or danger.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.reveals: Offer "Danger" beside "The blood shed in the struggle for independence" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.help: Tell the short story of the struggle for independence. Red remembers those who died.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.feedback: Red on our flag remembers the blood shed to make Kenya free.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.error: Thinks green stands only for trees or grass.

example.question: What does green stand for on the Kenya flag?
example.correct_answer: The land and its natural resources, including farming

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.cause: Green things the child knows are leaves and grass.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.reveals: Offer "Only trees" beside "The land and its natural resources, including farming" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.help: Show pictures of farms, forests and wildlife: all part of our land.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.feedback: Green stands for our land and all its natural resources.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.error: Puts the colours in the wrong order, often with green on top.

example.question: Which colour is at the top of the Kenya flag?
example.correct_answer: Black

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.cause: The child remembers the colours but not where each goes.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.reveals: Offer "Green" beside "Black" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.help: Colour a flag strip by strip from the top, saying "black, white, red, white, green".
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.feedback: From the top the flag is black, white, red, white, green.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.error: Thinks the white stripes are only spaces between colours with no meaning.

example.question: What do the white stripes on our flag stand for?
example.correct_answer: Peace

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.cause: Thin white lines look like borders in drawings.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.reveals: Offer "Nothing, they are gaps" beside "Peace" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.help: Point at each white stripe and say "peace". Ask why peace is placed between the colours.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.feedback: The white stripes stand for peace.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_CO.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.error: Thinks the national anthem is a song sung at any time, like a play song.

example.question: Is the national anthem sung while playing football at break?
example.correct_answer: No, it is sung at special occasions like assemblies and national holidays

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.cause: The child knows it as one more song learnt in school.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.reveals: Offer "Yes, any time" beside "No, it is sung at special occasions like assemblies and national holidays" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.help: List occasions on the board. Say: the anthem is for important moments.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.feedback: The national anthem is sung on special occasions, like assemblies and national holidays.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.error: Thinks you may keep walking or playing while the flag is raised if you are far away.

example.question: The flag is being raised and you are walking to class. What do you do?
example.correct_answer: Stop, face the flag and stand still

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.cause: Being far away seems to make it not matter.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.reveals: Offer "Keep walking" beside "Stop, face the flag and stand still" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.help: Practise in the field: when the flag goes up, everyone freezes and faces it.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.feedback: When the flag is raised, stop, face it and stand still.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.error: Thinks the flag can be put on the ground while folding it.

example.question: Can the flag touch the ground?
example.correct_answer: No, the flag should never touch the ground

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.cause: Other cloths are spread on the ground to fold them.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.reveals: Offer "Yes, while folding it" beside "No, the flag should never touch the ground" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.help: Fold a flag in pairs, held off the ground. Say: we show it respect.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.feedback: The flag never touches the ground. We hold it carefully.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.error: Thinks caps and hats may stay on during the anthem.

example.question: What do you do with your hat when the anthem is sung?
example.correct_answer: Take it off

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.cause: The child has not noticed others removing caps.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.reveals: Offer "Keep it on" beside "Take it off" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.help: Show a picture of an assembly with caps removed. Practise.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.feedback: Take off your hat or cap during the national anthem.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_NATIONAL_FLAG.FLAG_ET.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..error: Mixes up rights and responsibilities, calling doing homework a right.

example.question: Is doing homework a right or a responsibility?
example.correct_answer: A responsibility

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..cause: Both words are new and taught together.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..reveals: Offer "A right" beside "A responsibility" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..help: A right is what I should get; a responsibility is what I should do. Sort cards with the two words.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..feedback: Doing homework is a responsibility. Going to school is a right.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..error: Thinks a right means getting anything one asks for.

example.question: Is getting a new toy every week a child's right?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, I have a right to toys
example.correct_answer: No, toys are a want; rights are things like food, school and safety

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..cause: The child hears "my right" used to demand things.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..reveals: Offer "Yes, I have a right to toys" beside "No, toys are a want; rights are things like food, school and safety" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..help: Link rights to needs: food, shelter, school, care, safety. Wants are not rights.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..feedback: Rights are what every child needs to grow well, not everything we want.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..error: Thinks play is not a right because it is not work or learning.

example.question: Is play a child's right?
example.correct_answer: Yes, play is a right

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..cause: Children are often told to stop playing and work.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..reveals: Offer "No, play is wasting time" beside "Yes, play is a right" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..help: Say: play helps children grow and be healthy. Show the right to play on the chart.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..feedback: Play is a child's right. It helps us grow.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..error: Thinks children have only rights and no responsibilities.

example.question: Do children have responsibilities?
example.correct_answer: Yes, like obeying parents and doing homework

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..cause: Children are cared for by adults and see duties as adult things.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..reveals: Offer "No, only adults do" beside "Yes, like obeying parents and doing homework" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..help: List small responsibilities children already do. Praise them.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..feedback: Children have responsibilities too, like obeying parents and caring for their things.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_RIGHTS_AND_RESPONSIB..source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.error: Uses moving things (a parked lorry, a cow) as landmarks.

example.question: Which is a good feature to find the market: a bridge or a parked lorry?
example.correct_answer: A bridge

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.cause: The child names what caught his eye on the walk.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.reveals: Offer "A parked lorry" beside "A bridge" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.help: Ask: will it be there tomorrow? Good features stay in one place.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.feedback: Use features that stay in place, like a bridge or a hill, to find your way.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.error: Lists the right features but in the wrong order along the way.

example.question: From school you pass a river, then a church, then reach the market. What do you pass first?
example.correct_answer: The river

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.cause: The child remembers the features as a set, not as a sequence.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.reveals: Offer "The church" beside "The river" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.help: Walk a classroom path with cards in order. Then retell it in order.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.feedback: Say the features in the order you pass them.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.error: Thinks only buildings count as features, not hills and rivers.

example.question: Is a hill a physical feature?
example.correct_answer: Yes, a hill is a natural physical feature

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.cause: Directions given in town use shops and buildings.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.reveals: Offer "No, features are buildings" beside "Yes, a hill is a natural physical feature" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.help: Sort pictures into natural features and built features.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.feedback: Hills, rivers and valleys are physical features too.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.error: Gives directions without saying which way to turn.

example.question: How would you tell a visitor to find the market after the big tree?
example.correct_answer: At the big tree, turn left and walk to the market

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.cause: Young children assume the listener knows what they know.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.reveals: Offer "Go to the tree" beside "At the big tree, turn left and walk to the market" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.help: Play a directions game in class: the listener must find the place only from your words.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.feedback: Good directions name the feature and which way to turn.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_WAY.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.error: Thinks the only activity in a market is buying.

example.question: Name another activity in a market apart from buying.
example.correct_answer: Selling (bargaining, transporting goods)

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.cause: The child goes to market with a parent who buys.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.reveals: Offer "There is none" beside "Selling (bargaining, transporting goods)" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.help: Role-play a market: some sell, some carry, some clean, some buy.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.feedback: Many things happen in a market: selling, carrying goods, weighing and cleaning.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.error: Thinks prices in an open-air market are fixed like in a supermarket.

example.question: What is bargaining?
example.correct_answer: Talking with the seller to agree on a lower price

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.cause: Price tags in shops seem to be the rule everywhere.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.reveals: Offer "Paying the first price" beside "Talking with the seller to agree on a lower price" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.help: Act out a seller and a buyer agreeing a price for tomatoes.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.feedback: In many markets the buyer and seller talk to agree a price. This is bargaining.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.error: Thinks goods appear in the market without anyone bringing them.

example.question: How do cabbages get to the market?
example.correct_answer: Farmers or traders carry them by cart, boda boda or lorry

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.cause: The child sees only the final stall.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.reveals: Offer "They are already there" beside "Farmers or traders carry them by cart, boda boda or lorry" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.help: Trace a cabbage from farm to market with pictures.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.feedback: People carry goods to the market by cart, boda boda or lorry.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.error: Thinks nobody cleans the market and rubbish just stays.

example.question: Who keeps the market clean?
example.correct_answer: Cleaners employed by the county, and the traders

ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.cause: The child sees a busy market but not the cleaning at night.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.reveals: Offer "Nobody" beside "Cleaners employed by the county, and the traders" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.help: Show a picture of market cleaners and the fees traders pay.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.feedback: Cleaners and traders keep the market clean.
ENVI.G2.SOCIAL.OUR_MARKET.MARKET_ACTIVIT.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.error: Thinks the weather is the same all day once it is sunny in the morning.

example.question: It is sunny in the morning. Will it be sunny all day?
example.correct_answer: Not always: it can change in the afternoon

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.cause: The child notices the weather at one moment only.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.reveals: Offer "Yes, all day" beside "Not always: it can change in the afternoon" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.help: Record the weather at 8, 12 and 3 o'clock for a week. Compare.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.feedback: Weather can change during the day. Look again in the afternoon.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: There are a few white clouds. Will it rain?
example.correct_answer: Probably not: dark, heavy clouds bring rain

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.cause: Rain comes from clouds, so all clouds seem to bring it.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.reveals: Offer "Yes, clouds bring rain" beside "Probably not: dark, heavy clouds bring rain" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.help: Show pictures of light white clouds and dark rain clouds. Sort them.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.feedback: Dark, heavy clouds often bring rain. Light white clouds usually do not.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.error: Reads the wind symbol (curved lines) as rain or as nothing.

example.question: What does this symbol mean: curved lines blowing sideways?
example.correct_answer: Windy

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.cause: Lines are read as water falling.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.reveals: Offer "Rain" beside "Windy" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.help: Blow on a paper strip and draw what you see. Compare with the rain symbol of drops falling down.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.feedback: Curved lines blowing sideways mean windy. Drops falling down mean rain.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.error: Thinks mornings are the hottest part of the day because the sun has just come out.

example.question: When is it usually hottest: morning or afternoon?
example.correct_answer: Afternoon

ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.cause: The child links the sun appearing with heat.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.reveals: Offer "Morning" beside "Afternoon" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.help: Feel the ground or a wall in the morning and after lunch.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.feedback: It is usually hottest in the afternoon. Mornings are cooler.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.WEATHER.WEATHER_TIMES.M_E.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.error: Names the soil type by colour only (red soil, black soil) and misses how it feels.

example.question: How can you tell clay from sand?
example.correct_answer: By how it feels and whether it makes a ribbon

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.cause: Soils near home are named by colour.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.reveals: Offer "By colour only" beside "By how it feels and whether it makes a ribbon" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.help: Give two soils of the same colour that feel different. Do the ribbon test.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.feedback: Feel the soil and roll it. Colour alone does not tell the type.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.error: Thinks sand makes the longest ribbon because it has the most grains.

example.question: Which soil makes the longest ribbon?
example.correct_answer: Clay

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.cause: More grains seem to make more ribbon.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.reveals: Offer "Sand" beside "Clay" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.help: Roll wet sand and wet clay. Sand breaks; clay stretches.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.feedback: Clay makes the longest ribbon. Sand falls apart.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.error: Thinks clay has the biggest particles because it sticks in big lumps.

example.question: Which soil has the biggest particles?
example.wrong_answer: Clay, it is in big lumps
example.correct_answer: Sand

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.reveals: Offer "Clay, it is in big lumps" beside "Sand" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.help: Rub each soil between the fingers and look with a hand lens. Sand grains are big and seen.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.feedback: Sand has the biggest particles. Clay particles are too tiny to see.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.error: Thinks there are only two types of soil: sand and mud.

example.question: Name three types of soil.
example.correct_answer: Sand, clay and loam

ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.cause: Wet soil is called mud at home.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.reveals: Offer "Sand and mud" beside "Sand, clay and loam" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.help: Show three samples side by side and name each. Mud is wet soil of any type.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.feedback: The three types of soil are sand, clay and loam.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.SOIL.SOIL_KINDS.M_E2_SOIL.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.error: Thinks the moon makes its own light.

example.question: Does the moon make its own light?
example.correct_answer: No, it reflects light from the sun

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.cause: The moon looks bright like a lamp.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Yes, it shines at night" beside "No, it reflects light from the sun" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.help: Shine a torch on a ball in a dark room. The ball looks bright but makes no light.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.feedback: The moon does not make its own light. It reflects light from the sun.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.error: Thinks a mirror or shiny tin is a source of light because it shines.

example.question: Is a mirror a source of light?
example.correct_answer: No, it only reflects light

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Yes, it shines" beside "No, it only reflects light" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.help: Put a mirror in a dark box. Does it give light? Then add a torch.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.feedback: A mirror only reflects light. It is not a source.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.error: Thinks lights should stay on in the day so the room is bright.

example.question: It is a sunny day. Should the classroom lights be on?
example.correct_answer: No, open the windows and use daylight

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "Yes, it is brighter" beside "No, open the windows and use daylight" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.help: Switch the lights off and open windows. Can we still see? Say: saving electricity saves money.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.feedback: On a sunny day, switch off the lights and use daylight.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.error: Thinks the sun is the only source of light.

example.question: Name a source of light apart from the sun.
example.correct_answer: A bulb (a torch, a candle, fire)

ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.cause: The sun is taught first as the giver of light.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "There is none" beside "A bulb (a torch, a candle, fire)" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.help: Darken the room and light a candle and a torch.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.feedback: There are many sources of light: the sun, bulbs, torches, candles and fire.
ENVI.G2.NATURA.LIGHT.LIGHT_SOURCES.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.error: Thinks an open bucket stores water as well as a covered one.

example.question: Which keeps drinking water safe: an open bucket or a covered jerrycan?
example.correct_answer: A covered jerrycan

ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.cause: Water poured in clean seems to stay clean.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "An open bucket" beside "A covered jerrycan" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.help: Leave an open and a covered cup for a day. Look at dust and insects.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.feedback: Covered containers keep water safe from dust and insects.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.error: Thinks a jerrycan never needs washing because only water goes in it.

example.question: Should a water jerrycan be washed?
example.correct_answer: Yes, it should be washed often

ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.cause: The child cannot see the slime inside.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.reveals: Offer "No, only water goes in" beside "Yes, it should be washed often" and ask the child to choose.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.help: Shine a torch into an old jerrycan. Show the green slime. Wash it.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.feedback: Water containers need washing often to keep the water safe.
ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.source: To confirm by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher: a common error of young children, not traced to a study by the author.

ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.error: Thinks animals can drink any dirty water.

example.question: Do animals need safe water too?
example.correct_answer: Yes, dirty water can make animals sick too

ENVI.G2.RESOUR.WATER.WATER_STORAGE.M_E2_.cause: Animals drink from puddles, so it seems fine for them.
